input: reports/21/manual-review.json (8 items, awareness only; MR21-01 and MR21-07 given a second look)

summary.headline: 0 H/M/L. All five new findings are documentation / spec-conformance accuracy defects in UniPoolerV2 and story-051. None has a Law-1 attack path. Proposed labels are kept. MR21-01 and MR21-07 stay parked and are not promoted.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-22

classification.assetImpact: None. The comment is wrong, but the arithmetic is checked, so an out-of-range input reverts instead of wrapping.
classification.likelihood: n/a. r^2 * ~4e6 overflows 2^256 only when r > ~1.7e35 wei (1.7e17 sUSDS), far above sUSDS supply. A pair balance above uint112 also makes pool()'s sync() revert ('UniswapV2: OVERFLOW'). A caller-supplied hypothetical sUSDSIn that overflows only reverts a view call.

classifiedFindings.justification: The 'Overflow bound' NatSpec still bounds the checked product of _swapAmount by uint112 reserves and a balance-capped `a`. Since 267660b, quotePool feeds uint256 balanceOf values and an unbounded caller `a` into that product, so the stated premise no longer holds for the quote path. The conclusion that an out-of-range input reverts instead of wrapping is still true, because the multiplication is checked. Reaching the overflow region needs a pair balance about 30x above the uint112 cap and beyond total sUSDS supply. pool() itself still sizes from uint112 reserves after sync. The only effect is that a view call reverts on a hypothetical input. This is a comment-accuracy issue (QA/NC); there is no availability or value impact to support Low.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Restate the bound per call site. pool() uses uint112 reserves after sync. quotePool uses uint256 balances and a caller `a` and can revert on absurd inputs, which is acceptable for a view.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-23

classification.assetImpact: None from UniPoolerV2 code. With feeTo live, the factory mints feeTo about 1/6 of sqrt(k) growth since kLast at each mint/burn. That growth includes our swap fees and any donation folded in by sync(), because sync() updates reserves without touching kLast. This dilution is standard Uniswap V2 pair economics, applies to every LP, and is not caused or worsened by the pooler.
classification.assumptions: Mainnet factory feeTo = 0xf385...5f85 (live), per sanitizer verification

classifiedFindings.justification: The quotePool NatSpec says that if the protocol fee is on, the fee share is minted before ours and 'only raises our LP'. That conditional statement is correct. In V2 mint(), _mintFee raises _totalSupply before our liquidity is computed, so actual LP >= quoted LP and minLP remains a valid floor. The finding still has value because the pipeline premise in code-scan MR-004 ('feeTo is off') is false on mainnet, and any later reasoning about sync()/donation beneficiaries must allow for feeTo's roughly 1/6 cut of k growth. That matters for F-02-051. No code path loses value, no floor becomes unsafe, and no availability changes. This is a QA/NC premise correction. It is kept as Q, not dropped, because a downstream rationale was built on the false premise.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Change the NatSpec to state that feeTo is live on the mainnet factory and remove the hypothetical framing. Carry 'feeTo LIVE' forward as a pipeline premise. MR-004's conclusion survives; its reasoning does not.

classifiedFindings.label: F-01-051

classification.assetImpact: None on-chain. The hazard is to audit-ledger traceability only.
classification.likelihood: Moderate that a human closer is misled. The failure modes are fail-safe or noisy, never fail-silent (see justification).
classification.assumptions: A closer selects by the issueId string in story/commit/tests instead of by fingerprint

classifiedFindings.justification: Story-051, commit 267660b and two tests credit the sync-before-sizing fix to 'ycn20l24'. That ID is L-24 8511fd5206, a wont-fix about a dust pre-seed. The fix actually remediates L-25 8ec2be7d59. The canonical-pair change that closes Q-19 098396142d carries no label at all. I checked whether this could make a closer act on the wrong ledger entry. It could, but every misdirection fails safe or fails loud. (a) L-25 and Q-19 are not closed. They stay fix-pending, which is never suppressed, so they keep being rescanned. That is safe. (b) L-24 could be flipped from wont-fix to fixed. Both statuses are suppressed, and if L-24's still-live dust pre-seed (untouched by 267660b, see MR21-08) were seen again it would surface as a REGRESSION. That is a false alarm, not a hidden bug. No path silently suppresses a live finding, so there is no Law-1 hazard and nothing to support Low. There is a minor indirect risk: a reader who believes 'ycn20l24 was fixed' could drop the MR21-08 / L-24 cutover guidance (create-and-seed atomically, derive floors only from quotePool). The impact of skipping that guidance is already owner-accepted as 'mild inconvenience', and a keeper using quotePool refuses to pool on ts==0. This is a traceability and faithfulness defect: report it as F-01-051 at informational severity, visible to the owner, and do not bundle it into QA.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Amend story-051 and the test labels (UniPoolerV2.t.sol:1604, UniPoolerV2.fork.t.sol:126) to ycn20l25, and cite ycn20q19 for the canonical-pair check. Until then, the /ledger closer must select by fingerprint (8ec2be7d, 09839614) and never by 'ycn20l24'.

classifiedFindings.label: F-02-051
classifiedFindings.storyTag: story-051 (review/); related to L-25 8ec2be7d59 NatSpec half of the fix plan

classification.assetImpact: None from the code. The NatSpec mis-describes who benefits from an unsynced donation. The code behaves correctly: sync() folds the donation into reserves pro rata to all LPs. The pooler's LP mint never captures the donation, and feeTo later takes about 1/6 of the resulting sqrt(k) growth.
classification.likelihood: Low that an operator makes an unsafe decision from this text (see justification).
classification.assumptions: POL share of the pair is not guaranteed by code; it is an operational fact that can change if third parties LP

classifiedFindings.justification: 'The zap' NatSpec says an unsynced donation 'would be absorbed into our swap and LP mint', and that syncing gives it 'to the pair's LPs, overwhelmingly this contract's POL'. Both statements are imprecise. In V2, the router fixes amountOut from reserves, so a donation present at swap() only eases the k-check. It is then folded into reserves by swap()'s _update and accrues pro rata to every LP. It never enters our LP mint. 'Overwhelmingly POL' is a market-structure observation, not a code guarantee, and since feeTo is live (Q-23), about 1/6 of the k growth is diverted at the next mint/burn. I checked whether an operator could make an unsafe decision from this text. None of the decisions the text informs are unsafe. Keeping sync() and never calling skim() is correct whoever the beneficiary is. The only decision the misstatement could distort is a knowing, voluntary protocol transfer of value directly into the pair in the expectation of capturing it. Under the externally-derived-value principle, that would at worst be a misallocation of the protocol's own gift (leakage = non-POL LP share + feeTo cut), not an attacker-reachable value leak. No code path in UniPoolerV2 or the dispatch flow sends tokens to the pair outside swap/addLiquidity. A non-malicious owner would not lose funds to an adversary through this. It is a documentation-faithfulness defect introduced by L-25's NatSpec rewrite and does not affect the FIX-COMPLETE verdict on L-25's code. Report it as F-02-051 at informational severity, visible to the owner.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Rewrite the paragraph: 'without a sync, swap() folds the donation into reserves (pro rata to all LPs, less feeTo's protocol-fee share at the next mint/burn) while s, sized from stale reserves, no longer balances the legs'. Drop 'overwhelmingly this contract's POL' or mark it as an operational observation. Optionally correct the L-25 ledger title wording ('absorbed in swap()'). That edit is human-only.

classifiedFindings.label: F-03-051

classification.assetImpact: None. The deviation is a security improvement: the L-21 HookNotSet guard.

classifiedFindings.justification: Story-048 still says the mint path is kept 'verbatim' and 'identical' to BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch. Since 267660b, UniPoolerV2._dispatch adds the HookNotSet guard as its first statement, and story-051 supersedes the clause without amending or waiving story-048. The divergence is intended and safer, because it closes L-21's silent zero-mint-debt path, so Law 1 is not engaged. Law 2 does require the authoritative stories to agree with the shipped code. A later reviewer or agent grading against story-048 would flag the guard as a deviation, or might 'restore' verbatim parity. That is unlikely to happen without review, so this is informational. A related bookkeeping point: story-051 is still in review/ while its code has landed. Report it as F-03-051 at informational severity.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Add an explicit waiver of story-048's verbatim clause in story-051, or amend story-048 to reference it, naming the HookNotSet guard as the sole intended divergence. Move story-051 out of review/ once accepted.

manualReviewSecondLook.topic: Fresh DefaultDispatchHook / non-accruing hook bypasses the L-21 identity guard
manualReviewSecondLook.wouldBeIfPromoted: QA/Low at most (same impact tier as L-21: recoverable protocol-own mint-debt under-accrual, no attacker)
manualReviewSecondLook.reasoning: The guard compares by identity, so only the constructor-deployed DefaultDispatchHook trips it. Every bypass needs a deliberate owner action: deploying and installing a new no-op hook, or setRatio(0) on a mint-debt hook. Applying the Law-3 surprise test, a competent owner would not be surprised that installing a hook which does nothing accrues nothing. Both the contract NatSpec ('an owner who deliberately installs a freshly deployed DefaultDispatchHook opts out of the guard') and story-051 state this, and a test pins it. I looked for an accidental route. phStaging2 scripts only pass setHook either freshly deployed mint-debt hooks or pinned HOOK_* constants (DeployMainnetPromotionReady, DeployMainnetUniboostCutover, DispatcherReplace*), and DeployMainnetPromotionReady:2691 asserts dispatcher.hook()==hook after wiring. No script constructs or forwards a DefaultDispatchHook. A stale mint-debt hook still bound to BalancerPoolerV2 fails loudly (OnlyDispatcher). L-21's stated failure mode, setHook skipped or reordered, is fully closed. Keep this parked, and do not block proposing L-21 fixed. Optional hardening only: also require the hook to report dispatcher()==address(this), which would catch any foreign or no-op hook. This should not be filed.

manualReviewSecondLook.topic: Deliberate quote poisoning vs L-22/L-23 wont-fix rationale
manualReviewSecondLook.wouldBeIfPromoted: Low (same root cause and ceiling as L-22/L-23, POL-only, multi-block external requirements)
manualReviewSecondLook.reasoning: The root cause is unchanged from L-22/L-23: floors come from a spot quote and pooled value is POL only. L-22's triageReason does explicitly cover an adversary ('We're literally tolerating an attack of this size'), but its ~0.44*t*Delta bound is relative to the quote. If an attacker poisons the quote itself, the effective baseline moves, which is the same mechanism L-23 describes ('stale floor widens effective tolerance beyond t') and which the owner accepted. Two levers exist. (a) The swap lever, which predates 267660b: the attacker moves spot before the keeper quotes and holds that state until the keeper's transaction lands. That means carrying an open mispricing across the quote-to-execution latency, offered free to every arbitrageur, against a pair whose $1 PhusdStableMinter anchor arbitrageurs already use. If the attacker instead controls ordering in a single block, the case collapses to the in-block sandwich that L-22 accepts. (b) The donation lever, new in 267660b: a donation shifts the balance-based quote, but the donor loses the donated tokens to LPs, which are mostly POL. It is strictly dominated by the swap lever. Neither lever reaches user funds or rises above the Low ceiling already accepted twice. Re-filing would re-raise an owner wont-fix without new impact. Keep it parked, with the operational guidance (the keeper bounds floors against the $1 mint price / an off-chain reference, and checks balanceOf==getReserves when quoting). The human only needs to confirm that L-22/L-23 cover the deliberate case, or reopen. A reopen would be justified only if keeper cadence becomes multi-block-latent with spot-only floors and no reference bound.
